summary: Sidney Lee studied at the City of London School (~1872–1878) and Balliol College, Oxford (~1878–1882). He later held a post at Queen Mary University of London from circa 1913 to 1924.

Tibetologist and Buddhist studies scholar Siegbert Hummel studied at Tübingen, Rostock, Munich, and Leipzig (PhD 1932–1938), under Erkes, Schubert, Wedemeyer, and Weller. He was Curator of the Asian Department at the Grassi Museum of Ethnology (1947–1955).

A scholar of sinology and Buddhist studies, Siegfried Behrsing studied at Greifswald, Tübingen, and Leipzig (PhD 1924–1930). He held posts at Leipzig, the Ethnological Museum of Berlin, and Humboldt University of Berlin (Professor and Director, 1953–1969).

Indologist and linguist Siegfried Goldschmidt studied at Leipzig, Berlin, Tübingen (PhD 1867), Göttingen, and Paris under scholars including Weber, von Roth, and Benfey. He served as professor at the University of Strasbourg from 1871 and 1881.

Indologist Siegfried Lienhard studied at Vienna, Paris, and Stockholm. He held posts at Göttingen, Banaras Hindu University, Kiel University (Professor 1962–1968), Stockholm University (Professor 1968–1990), Collège de France, and the International Association of Sanskrit Studies.

Sieglinde Dietz is an indologist, Tibetologist, and Buddhist studies scholar. She earned her PhD at the University of Bonn by 1980 under Michael Hahn and Frank-Richard Hamm, and was affiliated with the University of Göttingen in 1990.

Linguist Siew-Yue Killingley earned an MA from the University of Malaya (~1964–1966) and a PhD from SOAS (~1969–1972). She taught at St Mary's College, Fenham (1972–1980) and the University of Newcastle (~1977–1984).

Linguist and indologist Sigmund Feist earned his PhD from the University of Strasbourg (~1884–1888) under Heinrich Hübschmann. He later served as Director of the Reichenheim Orphanage from 1906 to 1935.
Signe Cohen is a scholar of Indology and religious studies who studied under Ludo Rocher. She holds a post as professor at the University of Missouri.
Signe Howell, a religious studies scholar, studied at SOAS University of London (~1968–1972) and the University of Oxford (~1973–1980). She was appointed Professor at the University of Oslo in 1989.

Indologist Sigrid Westphal-Hellbusch earned her PhD at Humboldt University of Berlin (1935–1940), later teaching there and at Free University of Berlin (Professor 1964–1970). She directed the West Asian Department at the Ethnological Museum of Berlin (1970–1976).

Indologist and religious studies scholar Sigurd Lindquist studied at Uppsala University (1914–1932, PhD), where he was taught by Karl Ferdinand Johansson. In 1934, he became docent in the psychology and history of religions at Uppsala University.
Linguist and Indologist Silvia Luraghi completed her Laurea at Turin (1978–1982) and PhD at Pavia (1983–1987). She held academic posts at Turin (~1992–1998), Roma Tre (~1994–1998), and Pavia (~1998).

Specializing in philosophy and indology, Silvio Trovanelli completed a law degree at the University of Bologna by 1883. He subsequently served as docent of juridical philosophy at the University of Bologna.

Silvio Vita, specializing in Buddhist studies, Sinology, and Japanology, studied at Naples "L'Orientale" and Princeton. He held posts at "L'Orientale", Sapienza, Naples Federico II, Kyoto University of Foreign Studies, and directed the Italian School of East Asian Studies.

Linguist and Assyriologist Simo Parpola completed his PhD at the University of Helsinki (1961–1968) and studied at the Pontifical Biblical Institute and British Museum. He held posts at Heidelberg, Chicago, and Helsinki, where he became professor in 1978.

Indologist Simon Cubelic earned a PhD at Heidelberg and an MA at Humboldt. He held posts at the Heidelberg Academy of Sciences, Heidelberg University, and the University of Munich, and is attested as professor at Göttingen Academy of Sciences in 2026.

Indologist and linguist Simon Matthews Edwin Kempson studied at Cheltenham and Gonville and Caius College. He served as Headmaster of Bareilly College, taught at Cambridge (1879–1881), and was Professor of Hindustani at Staff College, Camberley (1882–1883).
Simon P. James is a scholar in philosophy and Buddhist studies. He held posts at Durham University as a tutor in philosophy (attested 2001) and lecturer in philosophy (attested 2013–2014).
Simon Winant works in Indology and linguistics. As of 2026, he is attested as a PhD student and faculty member at Ghent University.
